title: Decouple ingress/egress rates and bill-smoothing pilot for hosted per-token billing
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Many enterprise customers ask for clearer economics when mix of short input-heavy calls (embeddings, classification) and long output-heavy chat calls are both billed per-token. Current single-rate per-token billing causes unpredictable spikes and complicates negotiated minimums. This ticket pilots a decoupled IO billing model plus a short-term "bill-smoothing" mechanic (grace credits + paced floors) to reduce invoice volatility while preserving unit economics for Redwood.

Goal: Validate whether separating ingress (input) vs egress (output/streaming) token rates and offering a controlled smoothing mechanism (temporary credits to absorb bursts, + an adjustable minimum that ramps) reduces churn and sales friction for mid-market/enterprise customers without materially increasing unit cost.

Success metrics (primary):
- 10% reduction in customer-reported billing disputes for pilot cohort over 60d.
- <5% uplift to Redwood effective $/1000 tokens vs baseline (i.e., experiments should not lose money beyond tolerance).
- Sales acceptance: 3/4 pilot accounts sign renewed commitments that reference the new structure.

Secondary metrics:
- Latency of streaming/charged sessions (no negative impact).
- Observed behavioral change: average session output tokens / input tokens shift (indicates NLU misuse or gaming).

Scope of the pilot:
- Implement a rate table in the billing layer that surfaces two rates: ingress_rate and egress_rate. Streaming output tokens counted as egress; partial streaming (when client cancels early) prorated.
- Add a configurable "smoothing" profile for pilot customers: a grace credit pool that auto-applies to negative invoice deltas for first 30 days of a new contract, and a 3-month ramped minimum that phases in billing floors.
- UX: Billing page shows separated line items and a simple explainer. Sales gets a one-pager and a calculator.
- Acceptance gated by legal & security questionnaire review (enterprise asks about auditability and KMS handling of billing metadata).

Experiment design:
- Cohort: 7 existing enterprise accounts (voluntary) + 10 new signups from mid-market sales outreach. Controls: matched baseline group with similar usage volume.
- Duration: 90 days for behavioral data; billing smoothing active first 60 days, metric evaluation at day 30 and day 60.
- A/B elements: (A) ingress/egress split only; (B) ingress/egress + smoothing.

Implementation notes & trade-offs: 
- Trade-off 1: Complexity in billing engine vs transparency. We accept a small increase in billing derivation complexity to improve sales conversations. Billing logs must be fully auditable (exportable CSV) to satisfy auditors.
- Trade-off 2: Risk of gaming (clients crafting many small inputs to push egress). Mitigations: usage heuristics, fraud monitoring, and hard caps per-minute per-API-key during pilot.
- Trade-off 3: Accounting recognition — finance sign-off required for deferred revenue implications of grace credits.

Open questions: 
- What margin buffer is acceptable to finance when exposing differentiated rates? (Finance preference: no more than 3% effective unit economics degradation across pilot.)
- Do we automatically revert customers if smoothing leads to sustained higher consumption? Proposed: include a 30-day review clause.

Operational runbook (high level):
- Step 1: Create new pricing flags and rate fields in billing service (ENG).
- Step 2: Console shows line itemization and smoothing status (PM + Frontend).
- Step 3: Sales enablement materials + calculator (PM).
- Step 4: Legal/security questionnaire updates & IRB with Security for billing metadata (Security).
- Step 5: Launch pilot to cohort; monitor dashboards daily for first 14 days, then weekly.

notes: Pilot requires cross-functional sign-off (Finance, Legal, Security). Expect iterative updates to smoothing parameters based on early telemetry.
assumptions: Streaming token counting is stable across backends; no model-side changes required. Pilot customers agree to share anonymized invoice-level data for analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Billing line items visible in Console for pilot customers; invoices show separate ingress/egress rows; smoothing applied correctly for arm B; audit CSV export matches invoices for 3 sample customers.
audit_log_requirements: Exportable CSV with timestamped token counts, per-request attribution (request_id), rate_applied, and smoothing_credit_used. Retention 13 months.
implementation_risks: Potential for short-term revenue leakage from smoothing; complexity in reconciliation with accounting; risk of customers gaming split without throttles.
communication_plan: Pre-launch: targeted emails to pilot customers, sales training session, and a dedicated support Slack channel. Post-launch: weekly findings email to stakeholders, and a public pricing blog if we graduate experiment.
retrospective_plan: 30/60/90 day reviews; final decision rubric to either 1) roll to GA, 2) iterate parameters, or 3) sunset and revert to single-rate with learnings published.
customer_notes: Pilot onboarding checklist to include explicit opt-in consent for pilot billing model and a simple calculator showing projected invoices under both models.
regulatory_considerations: Finance to confirm VAT handling under split billing. Security to confirm billing metadata classification for EU customers.
